request.summary: Create an upbeat employee recognition wall for fictional Paper Kite Studio using an editable table of people, achievements, teams, quotes, and photos.
request.audience: Paper Kite Studio employees and visitors viewing shared workplace signage.
request.primaryGoal: Celebrate individual contributions through an editorial photo mosaic that stays readable and intentional across full-screen, wide-low, portrait, and square placements.

assumptions: Recognition order follows the editable datasource row order.
Pages rotate automatically when more people exist than the current surface can present legibly.
Missing or failed portrait URLs use a branded initials treatment instead of hiding the recognition.
The default light palette is inspired by a lively independent design studio rather than an existing customer brand.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The request explicitly requires four substantially different production ratios, so the photo-led editorial system must adapt its composition rather than scale one fixed canvas.

surfaces.purpose: Full-screen studio recognition wall with a dominant portrait and supporting recognitions.
Wide-low signage strip with a compact masthead and horizontal recognition rhythm.
Portrait display with stacked editorial tiles and a tall lead story.
Compact recognition tile that keeps one lead person and concise supporting context legible.

settings.purpose: Studio or organization name shown as the editorial masthead.
Message shown when a bound datasource has no valid recognition rows.
Controls the automatic page rotation interval.
Shows or hides optional employee quotes.
Selects the coordinated Light, Dark, or Custom studio palette.
Custom coral accent for lead recognitions.
Custom warm highlight color for achievement callouts.
Custom contrasting cool accent for mosaic variation.

dynamicText.fallback: At the readable minimum, retain the leading text and ellipsize only the tail.
dynamicText.rationale: The studio name is a first-viewport brand signal but must share the masthead with the wall title.

dynamicText.fallback: At the readable minimum, preserve one line and ellipsize the tail.
dynamicText.rationale: The editorial title establishes the recognition purpose without becoming a large dashboard header.

dynamicText.fallback: After two complete lines, ellipsize the remaining tail while preserving the full datasource value.
dynamicText.rationale: Names are a primary content surface and should remain substantially visible without crowding achievements.

dynamicText.fallback: Clamp after the surface-specific line allowance and continue the full achievement on a later curated recognition entry if needed.
dynamicText.rationale: Achievements carry the wall's meaning and receive more lines than secondary metadata.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize secondary metadata after one line while preserving it in the editable datasource.
dynamicText.rationale: Role and team orient the viewer but must not compete with the person or achievement.

dynamicText.fallback: Hide the tail after two complete lines; quotes are optional supporting texture.
dynamicText.rationale: Short quotes add personality but remain subordinate to the achievement.

states.expectation: One recognition expands into a deliberate full-composition feature rather than a stranded card.
Two recognitions form an asymmetric editorial pair with both achievements readable.
Five recognitions fill the primary mosaic without equal KPI-card repetition.
Seven recognitions paginate into balanced four- and three-person pages.
Missing and failed image URLs resolve to branded initials treatments without layout collapse or failed-request noise.
Very long names, studio title, roles, teams, achievements, and quotes remain contained with complete readable prefixes and safe descenders.
A bound datasource with no rows renders a quiet, intentional empty-state composition.
The final partial page remains balanced and visually intentional after timed rotation.
A datasource row edit updates the visible recognition without rebuilding the app.
The coordinated dark preset preserves the upbeat editorial character and contrast.
Processed row-array output normalizes to the same typed recognition model.

behaviors.expectation: Pages rotate on the configured interval, wrap circularly, and keep prime and partial counts balanced.
Editing a datasource row updates visible recognition content immediately.
Timed advancement reaches a composed final page without overflow or empty tile shells.
Paging shows every honouree exactly once per cycle, never renders an empty page, and returns to the first page after a full cycle.
An empty datasource still identifies the app and states why the surface is empty, in text legible at the declared viewing distance.

visualDirection.summary: A bright independent-studio recognition wall with editorial cropping, asymmetric rhythm, tactile paper-like color blocks, and achievements treated as headlines.
signatureChoices: One lead portrait breaks the rhythm while compact supporting recognitions alternate photo, color, and typography emphasis.
Warm coral, signal yellow, studio blue, and deep green create a multi-color print-editorial palette on a soft neutral canvas.
An offset vertical folio and small team ribbons replace the boilerplate's standard top header and page-dot treatment.
avoid: Equal KPI cards, a dark dashboard default, oversized marketing hero copy, rounded pill labels, and boilerplate page dots.

visualReview.intent: The result should read as a lively studio culture wall from a distance: people first, achievements second, metadata third, with each ratio feeling purpose-composed.
focus: Verify single, two-person, odd, prime, and final-page counts create intentional silhouettes without repeated equal-card geometry or dead zones.
Verify portrait crops stay useful, initials fallbacks feel designed, and broken URLs never show browser image icons.
Verify long achievements and names keep readable prefixes, complete line ink, and do not collide with role, team, quote, or folio elements.
Verify wide-low and square surfaces prioritize recognition content rather than allowing masthead or decoration to consume the canvas.
